item.title: Water Cycle With Exact Labels

turns.text: Make a 10-second widescreen water-cycle explainer with a friendly voice-over you write. Show water rising, clouds forming, then rain. Label those stages exactly “Evaporation”, “Condensation”, and “Precipitation”, in that order. No other on-screen text.

item.tests: Tests exact rendered labels, correct stage mapping, and coordinated original narration in a short explainer.

answer_sheet.Exact on-screen labels: Evaporation; Condensation; Precipitation. Use that capitalization and order, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Other text: No other on-screen text, including subtitles.

Water rises as vapor, clouds form, and rain falls, in that order.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create an exactly 10-second widescreen 16:9 educational water-cycle explainer. Friendly, clean colorful 2D animated infographic, easy for beginners to understand. A continuous landscape with a blue lake, green land, warm sun and sky. Locked wide camera, clear uncluttered composition. Three sequential stages, in this exact order: 0.0–3.3 seconds: sunlight warms the lake and delicate visible wisps of water vapor rise upward from the water. Display only the exact label “Evaporation” in large clear legible lettering. 3.3–6.6 seconds: follow the rising vapor as it cools and gathers into fluffy clouds. Replace the previous label with only the exact label “Condensation”. 6.6–10.0 seconds: the clouds release visible raindrops falling to the land and lake. Replace the previous label with only the exact label “Precipitation”. Each label must be spelled exactly as given, with no quotation marks, appearing only during its corresponding stage. No other on-screen text whatsoever: no title, subtitles, captions, credits, numbers, logos or extra labels. Include a warm friendly original English narrator, speaking clearly with a natural encouraging voice, paced to finish within 10 seconds. Exact voice-over: 'Sunlight warms water, and it rises as vapor. The vapor cools into clouds. Then water falls as rain, starting the cycle again.' Synchronize the narration with the three respective animated processes. Voice-over only, no singing, no background music. Show the full sequential rise, cloud formation, and rainfall clearly.
